fields.label: Your story
fields.sample:
It all began on an ordinary Tuesday evening, in a small bookshop in Kadıköy. Two hands reaching for the same book at the same moment, a shy smile and the words “You take it, I’ll wait”… One of us kept the book, the other the phone number.
Then came long walks, conversations that lasted until morning, cities we got lost in together. We became each other’s best friend; in laughter and in hard times, we were always on the same side.
One summer evening, a single question asked outside the bookshop where we first met changed everything. The answer was short: “Yes.” Now we want to write the most beautiful page of this story together with you.

fields.label: Thank-you message
fields.sample:
Thank you endlessly for being with us on this journey, for sharing our joy and for making this day unforgettable for us.
We’re so lucky to have you; here’s to meeting again on many more happy days.

elements.name: Haber metni
elements.text:
The puzzle their friends have talked about for years has fi­nal­ly been solved. The story began in a small book­shop in Kadıköy, with two hands reach­ing for the same book, and for seven years it dropped clue after clue: shared coffee orders, cities they got lost in to­geth­er, con­ver­sa­tions that lasted until morning.
According to the ex­perts, the hard­est ques­tion was asked one summer evening out­side that same book­shop. The answer was short­er than ex­pect­ed: three let­ters, one word. Close friends an­nounced “We solved it across ages ago,” while both fam­i­lies greet­ed the result with tears of joy.
The couple is plan­ning a big cel­e­bra­tion to share the happy result with their loved ones. Guests are kindly asked to bring a pen to the table and joy in their hearts. Inside: a cross­word, a word search, a sudoku and horo­scopes just for the guests; true to old news­pa­per tra­di­tion, the an­swers are print­ed upside down on the back page.
Word has it the couple kept the clues safe for years: their first movie tick­ets, notes tucked be­tween the pages of books, a col­lec­tion of mugs for two. Sources say the groom checked the ring in his pocket three times on the night of the pro­pos­al, and the bride smiled before an­swer­ing: “This would have been easier as a cross­word clue.” Their friends have re­port­ed­ly or­ga­nized a solv­ing race of their own for the wed­ding party.
A note from our puzzle desk: tonight’s only rule is to solve every ques­tion with a smile. Spare pens are wait­ing at the wel­come table for guests who forgot theirs; erasers will be handed out for wrong an­swers only. Good luck and have fun!
